summary: Knight-Hennessy Scholars is a leadership development programme for graduate students at Stanford University in the United States. Scholars study for a full-time Stanford graduate degree in any of Stanford's seven schools and also join leadership programming. The programme is open to applicants of any nationality. The 2026 cohort has 87 scholars. The award pays tuition for up to three years, a living stipend and an annual travel stipend.
eligibility_notes:
The programme has no restrictions on age, college or university, field of study or career goal. You do not need a nomination or endorsement from your institution, and there are no quotas by discipline, programme or world region. These rules are for the 2027 cohort and may change for later cohorts.

You must apply to, be accepted by and enrol in a full-time Stanford graduate degree programme (the page gives DMA, JD, MA, MBA, MD, MFA, MPP, MS and PhD as examples, and says the list is not complete). You must also meet one of four situations: you apply to the programme and to a Stanford degree at the same time and both start in the same year; you already hold an offer from a Stanford graduate programme that you deferred, and both start in the same year; you are a current Stanford graduate student adding a new full-time programme starting in the same year as the award; or you are a first-year Stanford PhD student and the award would start in your second PhD year.

You must have earned a US bachelor's degree, or its equivalent from a college or university of recognised standing, in January 2020 or later. Military service widens this window by two years (January 2018 or later). Current students are eligible if they will earn their first degree by September 2027. If your first bachelor's degree was earned more than seven years before your intended enrolment (2019 or earlier for autumn 2027), you are not eligible, even if you later earned another degree. Holding a graduate degree does not exclude you if your first bachelor's degree was earned in 2020 or later. For non-US degrees, you must meet the rules of your intended Stanford programme, and Stanford's Office of Graduate Admissions sets those rules.

Not eligible: the Honors Cooperative Program, the Master of Liberal Arts, the Doctor of Science of Law (JSD), the Master of Legal Studies (MLS), current Stanford PhD students adding an MA or MS in their own PhD discipline, and coterminal degrees (a current coterminal student is eligible only when applying to a new full-time programme through the external process, with the new programme and the award starting in the same year). Students already enrolled in a Stanford graduate programme in 2025 or earlier are not eligible for that programme.

Applicants with DACA status, no formal citizenship or other undocumented status may apply and enrol. There is no minimum grade average and no minimum test score set by the scholars programme, but your degree programme's own minimums apply. If your degree programme requires proof of English, you must send it to the scholars programme too.

Offers of the award cannot be deferred. If you are selected but cannot enrol that year, you must reapply for the year you will enrol.

First-year Stanford PhD students can combine the award with these fellowships: ARCS, Dissertation Completion Fellowship, Gerald J. Lieberman Fellowship, RAISE Doctoral Fellowship, SGF and SIGF. The CCSRE Graduate Fellowships and the Shoucheng Zhang Graduate Fellowship cannot be combined with it, and you may not drop them in order to apply.

Iran: from 24 August 2026, because of US Treasury (OFAC) changes, Stanford says it cannot file or process applications, accept fees or tuition, or provide certain educational services to people located in Iran, or ordinarily living there.
age_experience_notes: No age limit. No work experience requirement is stated. The first bachelor's degree must have been earned in January 2020 or later (January 2018 or later with military service), or be earned by September 2027.
funding_summary: The award is a fellowship paid directly to cover tuition and related fees, plus a stipend for living and academic costs, and an annual economy-class round trip to Stanford. New enrollees also get a one-time relocation stipend. Funding runs up to three years for the degree named in the initial admission letter, counted in quarters by degree type. Scholars who add another graduate programme may apply for more funding up to a three-year maximum, which is not guaranteed. Stipends are taxable.
programmes_note: Any full-time Stanford graduate degree programme in any of Stanford's seven schools. The page names DMA, JD, MA, MBA, MD, MFA, MPP, MS and PhD as examples. The page names the Business, Education, Engineering, Humanities and Sciences, Law, Medicine and Sustainability schools in its list of scholars by school. For an MBA, only the Round 1 deadline fits the scholars timeline. Excluded programmes are listed under eligibility.
institutions_note: Stanford University only. You apply to the scholars programme and, separately, to your chosen Stanford graduate programme, and you must receive an offer from that programme to become a scholar.

summary.detail: Full-time Stanford master's-type degrees. Funding covers up to 6 quarters (1 to 2 years) for MA, MBA, MFA, MPP, MS, JSM, MLS and LLM as listed in the funding table, and 9 quarters for a JD. Excluded: Honors Cooperative Program, Master of Liberal Arts, and MA or MS added by current Stanford PhD students within their PhD discipline. (The funding table lists the MLS and the eligibility page lists it as ineligible; the pages disagree, see notes.)

summary.detail: Full-time Stanford doctoral programmes. PhD and DMA: up to 12 funded quarters (9 academic quarters plus 3 summers), years 1 to 3; the degree programme's own funds apply from year 4. MD: up to 11 funded quarters (not the summer of year 1); the Medical School funds years 4 and 5. MD/PhD (MSTP): up to 12 quarters, years 1 to 3, degree programme funds from year 4. The Doctor of Science of Law (JSD) is not eligible.

benefits.limit_text: A fellowship paid directly to cover tuition and associated fees, up to three years depending on degree (up to 6 quarters for MA, MBA, MFA, MPP, MS, JSM, MLS, LLM; 9 for JD; up to 11 for MD; up to 12 for PhD, DMA and MD/PhD)
benefits.conditions: Covers the degree named in the initial admission letter. Scholars who add a further graduate programme may apply for more funding up to a three-year maximum; this is not guaranteed. Later years of long degrees are funded by the degree programme or the school.

benefits.limit_text: A stipend for living and academic expenses (room and board, books, supplies, instructional materials, local transport, reasonable personal expenses); amount not stated
benefits.conditions: Stipends are taxable and not subject to withholding, except for international students from countries without a tax treaty. The programme does not reimburse taxes.

benefits.limit_text: An economy-class ticket for one round trip between home and Stanford each year
benefits.conditions: Finalists' travel to the Immersion Weekend is also covered (airfare, lodging at Stanford, on-campus meals) within university guidelines.

benefits.limit_text: One-time relocation stipend (and/or technology purchases) for new enrollees
benefits.conditions: New enrollees only. Amount not stated.

benefits.limit_text: Supplemental academic enrichment funds in years 2 and 3, for example conference travel
benefits.conditions: Scholars must apply for these funds. Amount not stated.

benefits.limit_text: Health insurance is not mentioned on the funding page

requirements.text: Online scholars application, submitted in English through the online application system (email and post are not accepted). Contact details, biographical and demographic information, and explanations of your employment, activities and awards. It cannot be edited after submission except test scores, recommenders, resume and intended programme.

A separate application to your Stanford graduate degree programme, submitted by the earlier of that programme's deadline for scholars applicants or 1 December 2026. The programme's own application fee must be paid; the scholars programme cannot waive it.
requirements.conditional_rule: Not needed by applicants who already hold a deferred 2027 offer, or first-year Stanford PhD students starting the award in their second year

requirements.text: Resume: one page, US Letter size, legible font, reverse-chronological order, highlighting experiences, interests and academic record. No photos and no hyperlinks.

Scanned transcript for each institution attended for one academic year or longer (undergraduate and graduate). An unofficial transcript is accepted; if you cannot get one, use the self-reported transcript form. Transcripts must show any degree and its conferral date (otherwise add a diploma or similar). Documents in another language need an official English translation. There is no minimum grade average.

Two recommendation letters from people who know you well and can give specific examples (family members are not appropriate). Letters must be in English; a translation may be arranged by someone other than you, and the original and translation are uploaded as one document. You may not write, draft, edit, translate or submit the letter. Recommenders are registered in the online application and receive a personal link; use work email addresses where possible. Letters are due by the application deadline, but you must submit your own part on time even if letters are missing.

Three short answers: (1) short-term and long-term academic and professional intentions, 250 words; (2) a time you engaged with someone with a different perspective, acted with courage and fell short of expectations, 250 words combined; (3) eight unlikely but true facts about yourself, 150 words combined. Plus one essay of 550 words answering how the influences in your life have shaped you. Content must be your own work under the programme's AI-use policy.

Standardised test scores only if your Stanford degree programme requires them; the scholars programme sets no minimum. Submit by the later of the degree programme's deadline or the scholars deadline. New scores can be added through your application status page.
requirements.conditional_rule: if the graduate programme requires them

requirements.text: English proficiency results if your degree programme requires them. TOEFL is accepted by all Stanford graduate programmes, IELTS by most (not all), and PTE only by the MBA programme. The page gives typical minimums of IELTS 7 and TOEFL 90 for tests before 21 January 2026; its figure for later TOEFL tests (5.5) looks like an error, so confirm with your programme. Some departments accept scores up to 18 months old, others 24 months.
requirements.conditional_rule: if the graduate programme requires it

requirements.text: Video statement (about 2 minutes at most) recorded inside the online application, answering the prompt to teach something to your cohort. Your face must be visible; outside uploads are not accepted.

application_steps.title: Plan both applications and check eligibility
application_steps.detail: You make two separate applications: one to the scholars programme and one to your chosen Stanford graduate degree programme. Each should mention the other. Check the degree-date window and the list of ineligible programmes first. The scholars application opened on 1 June 2026 and its deadline for the 2027 cohort was 6 October 2026, 1:00 pm Pacific; the page now says it is closed and the 2028 cohort opens in summer 2027.

application_steps.title: Prepare and submit the scholars application
application_steps.detail: Complete the online form, one-page resume, transcripts, test scores if your programme needs them, two recommendation letters (register recommenders early), three short answers and the 550-word essay. There is no scholars application fee. Submit on time even if a letter is still missing; after submission you can only change test scores, recommenders, resume and intended programme.

application_steps.title: Submit your Stanford degree programme application
application_steps.detail: Apply separately and at the same time by the earlier of your programme's deadline for scholars applicants or 1 December 2026. A later submission can still be considered for the programme but makes you ineligible for the scholars award. For the MBA, only Round 1 aligns. Pay any fee your programme requires.

application_steps.title: Two separate committees review your applications
application_steps.detail: The scholars committee and your degree programme's committee review at the same time but independently and generally do not share materials. The scholars criteria are independence of thought, purposeful leadership and civic mindset. You must receive an offer from a Stanford graduate programme to be a scholar; applying does not hurt your chance of admission.

application_steps.title: Video statement by invitation, then finalist notice
application_steps.detail: About 500 applicants are invited on a rolling basis in January to record a video of up to two minutes, usually due 5 to 10 days after the invitation. All applicants get a status update on 27 January 2027, and up to 180 finalists are chosen. Not being invited does not mean a rejection.

application_steps.title: Online interview and Immersion Weekend
application_steps.detail: Finalists have an online interview in mid-February 2027 (up to 25 minutes, behavioural questions on the three criteria, recorded and judged by the selection committee). They then attend the Immersion Weekend on 5 and 6 March 2027 (faculty presentations, group activities, a group interview and social events), which is required unless unforeseen circumstances or immediate family obligations prevent it. Travel, lodging at Stanford and on-campus meals are covered within university guidelines. Finalists needing a visa to visit the US may request an invitation letter after selection.

application_steps.title: Scholars are notified
application_steps.detail: Scholars are notified on 16 March 2027. Degree programmes send their own decisions on their own timelines, from as early as December to as late as April.

application_steps.title: Enrol in your Stanford degree and join the programme
application_steps.detail: Scholars enrol in the full-time Stanford graduate degree and take part in leadership activities such as weekly storytelling (first year) and leading-yourself (second year) sessions, electives, retreats, KHeystone team projects and one global study trip of about a week. Scholars choose their level of participation depending on degree requirements. Offers cannot be deferred; if you cannot enrol in the selected year you must reapply.

application_steps.title: Funding years and taxes
application_steps.detail: Tuition is paid directly for the funded quarters listed for your degree. You receive the stipend, annual travel ticket, a one-time relocation stipend in the first year, and may apply for enrichment funds in years 2 and 3. Stipends are taxable and the programme does not reimburse taxes.
